name: trustcode
description: Security gate for your project: scans every file locally for SQL injection, exposed secrets, unsafe configuration and other vulnerabilities, highlights the exact code, and can block commits, pushes and releases. Also tracks what AI coding agents change.

commands.title: TrustCode: Ask Before Sending Code Again

trustcode.backendUrl.description: TrustCode server URL. Code is only sent here after you confirm. Use http://127.0.0.1:8000 with mode 'local' to keep code on your machine.

enumDescriptions: Verify and Session run on this computer with TrustCode's local engine. The code is not uploaded and no account is needed.
Verify and Session send the code you choose to the TrustCode server (trustcode.backendUrl) after you confirm. Needs an account.
trustcode.analysis.location.markdownDescription: Where the **Verify** and **Session** checks run. The Security tab always runs on this computer.

trustcode.engine.pythonPath.markdownDescription: Advanced. Full path of a Python interpreter that already has the TrustCode engine installed (`pip install "trustcode-worker[tools]"`). Empty: TrustCode uses the engine it sets up itself. Application-scoped so a workspace cannot point it at another program; a path inside the workspace is refused.

trustcode.engine.basePython.markdownDescription: Advanced. Full path of the Python (3.11 or newer) used to create TrustCode's private engine environment. Empty: the first suitable Python on your PATH.

trustcode.engine.registryLookups.markdownDescription: Local analysis: look imported package names up on PyPI / npm to detect packages that do not exist. Sends package names only, never source code. Off: package existence is reported as not checked.

trustcode.engine.runTests.markdownDescription: Local analysis: run the unit tests you supply with a verification inside the Docker sandbox (`trustcode-sandbox` image, no network). Without Docker they are reported as not run. Your project's own test suite is never run.

trustcode.mode.description: Only for server analysis (trustcode.analysis.location = server). account: sign in to a TrustCode server. local: single-user backend on this machine, no account (reads ~/.trustcode/local-secret).

trustcode.useLlmExplanations.description: Request LLM-written explanations (sends finding details to the configured LLM provider via the backend). Off by default.

enumDescriptions: All changes in the current tracking session
All files Git reports as changed
Every supported file in the workspace (asks first)
Syntax, static analysis and type errors.
Quick + security patterns, hardcoded secrets, dependency analysis, and consistency between files (imports, declared packages).
Standard + lookup of imported packages on PyPI / npm (the server contacts the registry with package names).
trustcode.verification.depth.markdownDescription: How thorough multi-file verification is. Every report lists the checks that did not run. Project tests are never executed for multi-file changes.

trustcode.verification.sendBaseline.description: Also send the previous version of modified files, so findings can be labelled “new in this change” or “already present before”. Off: the origin is shown as unknown.

trustcode.verification.includeRelatedFil.description: Also send unchanged files that a changed file imports, or that import a changed/deleted file, plus the nearest package manifest. Needed for cross-file checks.

trustcode.verification.maxFiles.description: Largest number of files one verification may send. More files in scope: you are asked, and the rest are listed as not analysed.

trustcode.verification.timeoutSeconds.description: How long to wait for each batch of a multi-file verification before giving up.

trustcode.autoVerify.onAgentFinished.markdownDescription: Verify unverified session changes when the agent reports that it finished (needs an agent hook; run **TrustCode: Agent Hook Setup**). Only sends to a server you approved with “don't ask again”.

trustcode.autoVerify.onInactivity.description: Verify after the configured period without file changes. This is an estimate that the agent finished, not a confirmation.

trustcode.autoVerify.onSave.description: Verify unverified session changes a few seconds after files are saved (never on every keystroke).

trustcode.autoVerify.onBatch.description: Verify once a batch of changed files has accumulated and settled.

trustcode.autoVerify.batchSize.description: Number of unverified changed files that counts as a batch.

trustcode.session.inactivitySeconds.description: Seconds without file changes after which a session is marked “possibly finished (estimate)”. 0 turns inactivity detection off.

trustcode.session.autoStartOnAgentSignal.description: Start a tracking session when an agent hook writes a “start” signal.

trustcode.session.useGit.description: Use Git (in trusted workspaces) to list files, honour .gitignore and read pre-session versions. Off or unavailable: files are scanned and snapshotted instead.

trustcode.session.exclude.markdownDescription: Glob patterns of files that are not tracked (generated files, dependency folders). Files ignored by Git are also left out when Git is used. Every excluded file that is not in a dependency folder is listed in the dashboard under “not tracked”.

trustcode.session.include.description: If set, only files matching these glob patterns are tracked (for example "src/**"). Empty: everything that is not excluded.

trustcode.session.extensions.description: If set, only files with these extensions are tracked (for example ".py", ".ts"). Empty: all file types, so configuration, dependency and migration changes are seen.

trustcode.session.sensitiveFiles.description: Files that are tracked (you see that they changed) but whose content is never sent to the server.

trustcode.session.maxFileSizeKB.description: Files larger than this are tracked by size and modification time only and are not sent. Separately, the server accepts at most 50,000 characters per file.

trustcode.session.retainRuns.description: How many verification reports are kept per workspace (stored locally in VS Code's workspace storage).

enumDescriptions: Only when a review is ready or an automatic run finished
trustcode.session.notifications.description: Which session events show a notification.

trustcode.scanner.path.markdownDescription: Command or full path of the local security scanner. Default: the scanner of the engine TrustCode set up, else `trustcode-scan` on your PATH. Application-scoped so a workspace cannot point it at another program.

trustcode.scanner.automatic.description: After the first scan, rescan automatically when files are created, changed or deleted (waits until changes settle; unchanged files are reused from the cache).

trustcode.scanner.settleSeconds.description: How long file changes must be quiet before an automatic rescan starts.

trustcode.scanner.scanSessionChanges.description: When a tracked AI coding session reaches a review point, scan the files it changed.

trustcode.scanner.onlineAdvisories.description: Look pinned dependency versions up in the OSV advisory database. Sends package names and versions only, never source code. Off: the dependency check is reported as skipped.

trustcode.scanner.timeoutSeconds.description: Longest time a scan may run.

trustcode.showExplanations.description: Show the longer “why it matters / suggested next step” text and explanation levels in the Verify and Session tabs. Off: findings show a title, location, severity and evidence only.

trustcode.scanner.scanGitHistory.description: During full and pre-production scans, also look for credentials on lines added in the last 500 commits. Slower on large repositories.

trustcode.scanner.scanOnStartup.description: Run a full local scan shortly after a trusted folder is opened, so findings and automatic rescans are available without clicking anything.

trustcode.updates.check.description: Check the project's public GitHub releases for a newer version, at most once a day. Sends no account or project data.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: TrustCode never executes workspace code. Its engine is installed outside the workspace and receives the code to check as data. In untrusted workspaces it does not run Git or the project scanner, and its security-relevant settings are application-scoped.
